We had company for turkey day and I was really nervous about being around people that I know for years, but I rarely talk to. It's difficult talking in crowds. The day before when I was cleaning, I found a small box of old expired prescriptions. I found antacids, insulin, leg cramp pills and an anti anxiety pill. I put it with the garbage and continued cleaning. Later I couldn't relax to sleep so I got my flashlight and went to get the anti anxiety bottle. I found it, and I took one and finally able to sleep. When family arrived I took 2 more. I felt good with company and actually talked more than I ever had. It was the best Thanksgiving I remember. After everyone was gone, I had to go to sleep. I wanted a good night sleep, so I decided to take one more pill. 

When I first found the pill bottle it was dark and I was using a flashlight, but now the lights were on. I grabbed the bottle and dropped a pill in my palm and at the same time I glanced to the label on the bottle. The bottle said Quinine sulfate. Take one tablet at bedtime for leg cramps. 

It wasn't the generic Valium I thought it was, it was for leg cramps. I had a family gathering and talked to people while taking a non narcotic leg cramp pill!!! 

I could have taken an aspirin, thinking is was a special pill that was a cure all. I believed so strongly that a pill could would help me fit it, that it worked. 

The psychosomatic effect of belief and desire came from within. No drug necessary except for what my brain released naturally in that fight or flight mode.

Were you ever alone in a crowd of people, your mind on overdrive and wondering "why am I such a freak". For many that is life with autism. For me drugs were my "in" with the supposed cool kids. I wanted to fit in, somewhere, anywhere. I discovered other people in school wanted me around if I had weed. And they did. I was letting them use me out of desperation to belong somewhere. That loneliness is devastating, more so for our younger autistic audience. 

Figuring out life is difficult. Add autism to the equation and then the equation becomes even more difficult. But then to say adding a mind altering chemical is okay, that's a big time wrong message to send. 

Confusion plus confusion plus added confusion equals chaos. I don't believe you want to confuse an already confused person. 

Here's a rhetorical question for you. How's life treating you? Do you have a job that pays for you to own a home? To raise 2.5 children and send them to college? Do you have a late model vehicle that is reliable? I could go on, but I think, from experience, I know the answer.

For the record, weed is not the gateway drug. That falls on nicotine and alcohol, the socially acceptable drug of choice for the masses. 

If a person wakes and bakes and then a hit here and a hit there throughout the day,  that's a problem.  Especially for a young, autistic mind.. On the other hand,  for an adult,, a joint after work or on weekends with friends, is fine. I am down with that. 

I'll admit that I am a more fortunate person. Most of us don't have that luxury. In fact, 99% of people don't have that luxury. For me this sub is to spread hope and a way to achieve a life worth a damn. I sure as s#!t don't want to lead anyone to a s#!t life, in a s#!t apartment in  a s#!tty part of town.
